summary.name: Intelligent agents guided by LLMs
summary.one_liner: A blog post presenting a small from-scratch Python library for building LLM-controlled agents that reason in a Thought/Action/Observation loop, inspired by langchain.
use_cases: Learning how an LLM agent works internally
Building a simple agent that searches Google
Creating an agent that executes Python code in a REPL
Searching Hacker News with an LLM agent
summary.what_it_does: The post describes a small library for building agents controlled by LLMs, written to be easier to understand than langchain. The agent runs a loop of Thought, Action, Observation, where the Thought and Action come from the LLM and the Observation comes from a tool. Tools are small Python classes with a name, a description, and a use(input_text) method. The author has implemented tools for Python REPL execution, Google search, and Hacker News search. The loop stops when the agent produces a Final Answer. To prevent the LLM from hallucinating observations, the author passes a stop pattern on "Observation:" so the real tool output is inserted instead.
notable: Deliberately minimal, built from scratch to be understood in few lines of code
Uses a stop pattern on 'Observation:' so real tool results replace hallucinated ones
Tools are simple Python classes implementing use(input_text) -> str
Injects today's date into the prompt to stop the LLM rejecting recent information
caveats: The author states the agent is far from perfect and fails a lot
Google search relies on SerpAPI as shown in the example tool code
Relies on an LLM API such as OpenAI for generation
